summary: Initial scoping call for embedding & rerank pilot. Customer is evaluating where to run embeddings and reranking (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key concerns: tail latency at high fanout, embedding dimensionality vs storage cost, vector DB integration (we run hybrid search+rerank), security/compliance and VPC options. Agreed next steps include benchmarks, cost model, and sharing security docs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-08-21 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jamie Lowe (Needle Head of Search), Priya Desai (Needle ML), Mark Soto (Needle Infra), Ana Torres (Product)
Shared: deck link: https://redwood.example.com/deck (redwood-hosting-options), bench sheet: https://sheets.example.com/needle-bench (sample)

[00:00] Alex Kim (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro: I'm Alex, AE on the retail practice, Samir is our SE who'll run through perf and architecture. Would you like to intro on your side?
[00:18] Jamie Lowe (Needle): Sure, I'm Jamie, head of search at Needle. We power recommendations and onsite search, lots of SKUs, around 30M products, but product variants and images make indexing heavy. Today's call is to figure out where to run embeddings and rerank for a hybrid search stack.
[00:36] Priya Desai (Needle): Hi, Priya here, I own embeddings and ranking models. Our current flow: embed at ingest into Milvus + store vectors, fanout top 100, then run a rerank model that calls a text generation model for context-aware scoring on the top results. We're hitting tail latency spikes under sale traffic.
[01:02] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Thanks. So you said Milvus today. Are you open to using a hosted vector DB or Redis for the fanout or do you want to keep Milvus?
[01:15] Priya: We're leaning to keep Milvus for persistence, but we are open to caching layers. The big question: should embeddings and rerank be on Redwood hosted api, Redwood dedicated, or our on-prem/private? Tradeoffs for us are cost, latency and security.
[01:34] Alex: Great. At a high level, common patterns: hosted (fast to try), dedicated (predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale), private (VPC or on-prem for strict compliance). For rerank we often place the lightweight ranking model in the same network as the vector DB to avoid network fanout latency, and use Redwood for high-throughput embedding + fallback.
[01:58] Jamie: When you say "place in same network" — do you mean Redwood Dedicated can be peered into our VPC?
[02:05] Samir: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private routes, we can also do Private (customer-managed control plane) if you need air gap. There are different operational models — dedicated is a Redwood-managed GPU pool in your region with VPC connectivity.
[02:22] Mark Soto (Needle Infra): Important: we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and key management via our KMS (HSM). SOC2 is a must.
[02:33] Alex: Understood — we have SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes, we'll share the security deck.
[02:40] Ana Torres (Product): From product POV we care about accuracy. We saw drop at 768 dims vs 1536, but cost doubles. Want to see actual delta in rerank uplift vs cost.
[02:53] Samir: Quick Q around throughput: what's your target p95 tail latency during peak? And qps?
[03:00] Priya: Baseline: 1k QPS on read path during peaks, with spikes to 6-8k for 5-10 minutes. Target p95 for rerank < 250ms if possible.
[03:12] Samir: That's a pretty tight SLA for a complex fanout+rerkank flow. Our playbook: reduce network fanout by sharding + colocating rerank, prefix / KV caching for repeated queries, and use smaller dimensional embeddings + rerank model to trade accuracy vs cost. Also batching and continuous batching at the runtime helps throughput.
[03:34] Jamie: You mentioned continuous batching — is that in Hosted? Does it add latency?
[03:40] Samir: It's in the runtime across all deployment modes. For hosted we default to latency optimized policies which keep batch windows small; dedicated can be configured to favor throughput with slightly higher p99. We can tune it.
[03:52] [05:12] Priya: Slight off note, we currently use openai text-embedding-ada for embeddings and a small BERT ranker for rerank. Open to specialized embed models. What models do you recommend?
[05:24] Alex: For embeddings we recommend trying a 1024-dim model for a first pass — many customers find a sweet spot between 768 and 1536. Redwood offers curated open models and we can run A/B evals. Also quantization options (8-bit, 4-bit) to reduce storage cost on Dedicated.
[05:44] Jamie: Any concerns around quantization impacting rerank accuracy?
[05:50] Samir: Yes, quantization can impact nearest-neighbor recall; it depends on embedding distribution. We can provide eval harness and quality monitors. For rerank, because you rerank top-K with a more expensive model, small recall loss can be masked, but it's workload dependent.
[06:18] [06:45] Mark: Ok network question: if we do dedicated with VPC peering, what about egress cost and cross-az bandwidth?
[06:53] Samir: With peering, traffic stays in-region; egress costs vary by cloud. Dedicated customers often show lower overall egress since we co-locate rerank and use caching. We'll include estimated egress numbers in the cost model.
[07:12] Priya: We do a hybrid search: vector store -> dense retrieve top 200 -> textual rerank -> business rules. Our biggest pain is tail latency when product launches spike. Would Redwood help smooth that?
[07:28] Alex: Yes, with autoscaling and burst capacity options we can spill to higher-capacity pools or fallback to cheaper model variants. Also automated fallback to a higher-latency but cheaper path if capacity constrained.
[07:40] Jamie: How are embeddings stored? Do you recommend storing the full float vectors in our vector DB or using Redwood's cache?
[07:48] Samir: Persist in your vector DB for durability; use Redwood prefix/KV cache for hot documents to speed retrieval. Some customers store 8-bit quantized vectors in DB and use a small-hot-cache for exact results.
[08:05] [09:02] Priya: For rerank costs — we do a 2-stage; cheap scoring then a GPT-style scoring step for top 10. If we move the GPT rerank to Redwood Hosted, latency kills us. But Dedicated or Private might be ok.
[09:15] Samir: Exactly — Hosted has extra network hop. For sub-200ms p95 rerank we'd recommend Dedicated in same cloud region and peered network or Private for on-prem.
[09:30] Ana: For pilot, what's the minimal scope to validate?
[09:34] Alex: A typical pilot: 1) share a 1k-doc eval set + query trace; 2) Redwood runs embedding variations (768/1024/1536) and rerank flows with dedicated bench; 3) measure recall/precision + latency + cost per 1M queries; 4) run a short smoke test at 10k QPS to observe tail.
[09:55] Priya: That sounds workable. How long to run the bench?
[09:59] Samir: We can run the A/B pass in 3-5 days once we have data; the 10k QPS smoke is a dedicated provisioning and takes about a day with planning.
[10:10] [10:40] Jamie: Security — our procurement requires SOC2, RBAC, audit logs, SSO, and KMS. Any blockers?
[10:50] Alex: No blockers. Redwood has SOC2, SSO/SAML support, RBAC in console, audit trails, and we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. We'll attach artifacts.
[11:05] Mark: One thing — our firewall only allows outbound to certain IP ranges. Can we get static egress IPs?
[11:12] Samir: Dedicated provides static egress IP ranges for peered customers; we can document the ranges. For Private/on-prem it's fully customer-controlled.
[11:25] [12:00] Priya: Let's talk numbers: approximate cost per 1M rerank calls for: hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[12:12] Alex: We'll provide a 3-tier cost model with ballpark numbers. Hosted is usually highest per-unit but lowest up-front. Dedicated amortizes costs and is cheaper per-1M at scale. Private has license/platform costs but gives you control. We'll email a detailed sheet.
[12:30] Samir: Also factor in quantization and batching — 4-bit quantization on embeddings reduces storage/cost but needs eval.
[12:40] [13:00] Jamie: For vector DBs, you said caching layer — can Redwood integrate with our Milvus and provide a cache or should we change DBs?
[13:08] Samir: We integrate with Milvus, Pinecone, Qdrant, Redis, etc. We usually recommend preserving your persistent DB and adding a hot cache (Redis or in-runtime KV). We can also do hybrid topK where we do metadata filtering in DB and distance sim in Redwood if needed.
[13:30] Priya: Any known issues with sharding and consistent ranking? We sometimes see skew across shards in Milvus.
[13:40] Samir: Shard skew can impact recall. Mitigations: smart routing, rerank normalization, or cross-shard fanout with corrected scoring. Our routing policies can help target shards predictively.
[13:58] [15:00] Alex: Quick run-through of pilot timeline: week 0: data share and config; week 1: A/B eval runs; week 2: smoke benchmark and ops validation; week 3: decision on host mode and initial roll.
[15:20] Ana: Ok. One more: how does Redwood monitor quality drift? We need alerts for embedding regressions after deploys.
[15:29] Samir: We have quality monitors tied to prompt sets/evals and regression alerts. We can wire those to Slack/email.
[15:40] Priya: Oh — a practical question — do you recommend storing per-product metadata together with vector or separate?
[15:48] Samir: Store minimal metadata in vector DB to filter, keep heavier attributes elsewhere. Filtering on metadata reduces fanout.
[15:58] [17:00] Jamie: Anything you saw in our description that would block a pilot?
[17:05] Alex: No blockers — we just need data and confirmation on compliance channels. We'll send security pack and cost model.
[17:12] Mark: For the 10k QPS smoke are there safety limits? We might simulate user behavior around launches.
[17:19] Samir: We can simulate realistic traffic patterns, including spike shapes. We'll coordinate with you on allowed IPs and test windows.
[17:28] [18:00] Priya: On evaluation metrics, apart from recall/precision and p95 latency, add business metrics like conversion uplift and click-through so we can justify costs.
[18:10] Alex: Agreed. We'll add those to the bench sheet.
[18:18] Ana: Great.
[18:20] Alex: Recap of next steps: Alex sends cost sheet and SOC2 pack, Samir schedules bench and runs smoke test, Priya shares queries and eval docs, Mark confirms VPC/firewall requirements. Any objections?
[18:38] Jamie: None. Looking forward.
[18:42] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the attachments.
[18:48] End of meeting.
